newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Energy sees earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: FCL Energy sees earnings rise.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy said on Wednesday that production, earnings and cash flow were expected to rise as the Maui F Sands oil comes into full production in October.
The Canadian operations would build on their quality assets to grow production, cashflow and returns, FCL Energy said.
In New Zealand, the operational outlook for 1997 was positive.
The focus would remain on optimising output from existing fields, reducing costs and realising the potential of undeveloped exploration lands.
FCL Energy said oil and gas production rose by 23 percent to 41.5 million barrels of oil equivalent over the year to June.

In Brunei, where it has secured offshore exploration rights to 800 square kilometres, the Maharaja Lela 3 well was spudded in May with hydrocarbons, both oil and gas, being encountered in a number of reservoir sequences.

"It is expected that the partners will proceed with the development of this gas/condensate field within the next six to nine months. If the project proceeds, it is likely to take at least two years to bring into production," FCL Energy said.

FCL Energy earlier announced a net profit of NZ$57 million against $64 million a year earlier. Increased oil and gas production, combined with higher oil prices, lifted operating cashflow by 26 percent to NZ$351 million.
Funding costs fell, reflecting the reduction of debt as a result of receipt of an instalment from Methanex in December and a stronger operating cashflow.

An NZ$8.0 million tax credit was mostly the result of the expensing of NZ$34 million of exploration costs in Brunei and the $16 million writedown of Four Bluff in the U.S. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
